Solve this benchmark problem `regex-redux` in JavaScript.

# regex-redux

Read a FASTA-formatted DNA sequence from standard input and reproduce the
Computer Language Benchmarks Game regex-redux benchmark.

1. Read all of standard input. The original length is the total number of
   bytes read.
2. Remove every FASTA header line (matching the regex `>.*\n`) and every
   remaining newline (`\n`). The result is the stripped sequence; its
   length is the stripped length.
3. Count the non-overlapping matches of each of these nine regular
   expressions in the stripped sequence, in this exact order, and print
   the pattern, a single space, then its count, one per line:
       agggtaaa|tttaccct
       [cgt]gggtaaa|tttaccc[acg]
       a[act]ggtaaa|tttacc[agt]t
       ag[act]gtaaa|tttac[agt]ct
       agg[act]taaa|ttta[agt]cct
       aggg[acg]aaa|ttt[cgt]ccct
       agggt[cgt]aa|tt[acg]accct
       agggta[cgt]a|t[acg]taccct
       agggtaa[cgt]|[acg]ttaccct
4. Apply these substitutions to the stripped sequence, in this exact
   order, replacing every match of the left regex with the right text:
       tHa[Nt]            -> <4>
       aND|caN|Ha[DS]|WaS -> <3>
       a[NSt]|BY          -> <2>
       <[^>]*>            -> |
       \|[^|][^|]*\|      -> -
5. Print an empty line, then the original length, the stripped length, and
   the length of the sequence after all substitutions, each on its own
   line.

Matching is case-sensitive. Print nothing else.

## Input
A FASTA-formatted DNA sequence on standard input.

## Output
```
agggtaaa|tttaccct <count>
[cgt]gggtaaa|tttaccc[acg] <count>
a[act]ggtaaa|tttacc[agt]t <count>
```
